public_rationale: Marcus says what people should expect, rather than making a definite nonarrival forecast. He also leaves 'any time soon' undefined. Treating October 2026 as his deadline or scoring subsequent nonarrival would add commitments he did not make. The wording therefore does not support a fair binary outcome assessment.
limitations: This decision makes no finding about whether Level 5 driving had arrived by the evaluation date.
No external evidence search was conducted because deployment records cannot define the missing predictive commitment or deadline.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Fully autonomous Level 5 driverless cars that safely go from any point A to any point B will not arrive any time soon.

statement.excerpt: More than that we just shouldn’t expect fully autonomous (Level 5) driverless cars—safely taking us from any old point A to any old point B—any time soon.
statement.document_title: Will Tesla ever “Solve” Full Self Driving?

from_speaker: safely taking us from any old point A to any old point B
our_interpretation: The statement advises restraint in expectations about unrestricted Level 5 driving.
I do not replace 'shouldn’t expect' with a categorical prediction that the technology will not arrive.
The phrase 'any time soon' supplies no fixed deadline. The evaluation date does not establish one.
criteria.support_condition: No objective support condition follows from the wording without adding a predictive commitment and a time window.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No objective contradiction condition follows from the wording without deciding what expectation was ruled out and when arrival would count as soon.
